name: Vanadium
occurrence: Found combined in about 65 different minerals and in fossil fuel deposits; extracted mainly as a by-product of iron ore processing.
majorUses: Vanadium redox flow batteries for grid energy storage
notableCharacteristics: Its compounds famously display a whole rainbow of colours depending on oxidation state — from violet (+2) to green (+3) to blue (+4) to yellow (+5).
whyHere: Vanadium has five accessible 3d/4s electrons, giving it an unusually wide range of stable oxidation states — which is exactly why its compounds shift through so many different colours in solution.
didYouKnow: A single vanadium solution can be made to cycle through four different colours just by adding a reducing agent step by step — a classic 'rainbow tube' demonstration in inorganic chemistry.
genZNote: One element, four oxidation states, an entire colour palette. The mood ring of the periodic table.
